title: RNG's Ascent: Why the Green Gas Market is Gearing Up for a Massive Decade
summary: The global renewable natural gas (RNG) market is projected to skyrocket, more than doubling from $14.87 billion in 2024 to $31.55 billion by 2034, driven by an 8.32% compound annual growth rate. This significant expansion is largely fueled by a global surge in environmental consciousness and a push towards sustainable energy solutions.
content:
In an era increasingly defined by the urgent pursuit of sustainability, a quietly powerful player is making significant waves in the global energy landscape: Renewable Natural Gas (RNG). This 'green gas,' purified from organic waste, is rapidly moving beyond a niche solution; new data reveals it's on the cusp of an explosive decade of growth.

A recent report from Zion Market Research, released on July 20, 2026, highlights this remarkable ascent. The global RNG market, valued at $14.87 billion in 2024, is projected to more than double, reaching an impressive $31.55 billion by 2034. This signifies a robust compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 8.32%, indicating accelerating adoption across industries and nations.

What’s fueling this expansion? Primarily, a burgeoning global environmental awareness is compelling both consumers and corporations to seek cleaner energy alternatives. Governments worldwide are also implementing policies and incentives that champion renewable sources. For companies, embracing RNG isn't just about compliance; it's a strategic move to enhance their ESG (Environmental, Social, and Governance) credentials and meet growing stakeholder demands for sustainable operations.

RNG stands out for its unique ability to tackle two pressing issues: waste management and clean energy generation. By capturing methane from sources like landfills, agricultural waste, and wastewater treatment plants, and upgrading it to pipeline-quality natural gas, RNG transforms a potent greenhouse gas into a valuable, versatile fuel. Its applications span from powering heavy-duty transportation fleets to providing industrial heating, offering a direct, drop-in replacement for conventional fossil natural gas.

As the world grapples with climate change, the rise of the RNG market signals a critical shift. It's a testament to how innovative waste-to-energy solutions can not only decarbonize our economy but also create a more circular and sustainable future, solidifying RNG's place as an indispensable component of the clean energy transition.
keyTakeaways: The Renewable Natural Gas (RNG) market is projected to more than double in the next decade, growing from $14.87 billion in 2024 to $31.55 billion by 2034.
This significant growth is primarily driven by increasing global environmental awareness, supportive government policies, and corporate demand for sustainable ESG solutions.
RNG effectively converts organic waste methane emissions into a versatile, pipeline-quality fuel, addressing both waste management and clean energy generation challenges.
author: Zion Market Research

title: Kinaxis Supercharges Strategy with Veteran Finance Chief Herb Yeh in Dual Role
summary: Kinaxis, a leading supply chain planning software company, has appointed seasoned corporate finance veteran Herb Yeh as its new Chief Financial Officer and Chief Strategy Officer. This strategic dual role leverages Yeh's 25 years of experience in growth, M&A, and transformation to drive Kinaxis's expansion and solidify its market leadership in the critical supply chain sector.
content:
Kinaxis, a pivotal player in global supply chain planning, has just announced a significant bolstering of its executive team with the appointment of Herb Yeh as its new Chief Financial Officer and Chief Strategy Officer. This dual role underscores a strategic move by the Ottawa-based software leader to tightly integrate its financial stewardship with long-term growth initiatives, especially pertinent in an era where supply chain resilience is paramount.

Yeh arrives at Kinaxis bringing over 25 years of extensive experience in corporate finance, with a distinguished career primarily focused on high-growth enterprise software companies. His expertise spans crucial areas including navigating periods of rapid expansion, orchestrating strategic mergers and acquisitions, and driving significant organizational transformations. This deep well of knowledge positions him uniquely to steer Kinaxis through its next phase of innovation and market penetration.

In a world still grappling with the complexities of disrupted supply chains and an accelerating demand for real-time strategic insights, Kinaxis's solutions are more critical than ever. Yeh’s proven track record in optimizing financial performance while simultaneously shaping strategic direction will be invaluable. His leadership promises to enhance Kinaxis’s financial agility and fortify its competitive edge, particularly as the company continues to expand its global footprint and innovate its Rescale platform to meet evolving market demands.

This appointment signals Kinaxis's unwavering commitment to aggressive growth and strategic market leadership. By entrusting Yeh with both financial oversight and strategic vision, the company is clearly betting on a unified approach to capitalize on emerging opportunities and navigate potential economic headwinds, ensuring its continued dominance in a vital sector.
keyTakeaways: Kinaxis has made a significant executive appointment, bringing Herb Yeh on board as both CFO and CSO.
Yeh's 25+ years of experience in corporate finance, growth, M&A, and strategic transformation in enterprise software will be crucial for Kinaxis's future.
This dual role signals Kinaxis's commitment to integrating financial strategy with aggressive growth and market leadership in the evolving supply chain landscape.
author: Business Wire

title: Reins Unlocks New Equity Model for Canadian Businesses, Safeguarding Ownership
summary: Reins, a pioneering US technology firm, is expanding into Canada, offering private businesses an innovative way to retain top talent and plan for succession. Its alternative equity solutions allow owners to incentivize key employees with ownership-like benefits without diluting their stake, building on proven success in the US market.
content:
LAS VEGAS – July 20, 2026 – Reins, a pioneering tech firm known for its innovative approach to business equity, is officially crossing the border, bringing its unique solutions to Canada. Following significant US success, the company aims to empower privately owned Canadian businesses with tools designed to navigate crucial challenges like employee retention and succession planning.

For years, private business owners have grappled with a delicate balancing act: how to reward and retain top talent, or orchestrate a smooth leadership transition, without resorting to traditional, often dilutive, equity schemes or outright sale. The standard playbook frequently demands sacrificing control, a prospect many independent entrepreneurs rightfully hesitate to embrace.

Reins steps into this void with a compelling alternative. Their technology-driven platform provides sophisticated ‘synthetic equity’ solutions, allowing owners to create powerful incentive programs – like profit-sharing or performance units – that mimic ownership benefits for key employees. Crucially, original owners retain full control and equity in their core business. It’s a game-changer for building lasting value and a loyal team without selling off pieces of the enterprise.

The expansion into Canada is timely, addressing a growing demand within the country's vibrant, yet often underserved, independent business sector. Canadian SMEs now gain a powerful new ally in securing their future, whether by incentivizing next-generation leaders or creating attractive packages that compete with larger corporations for talent. Reins' approach facilitates smoother paths for business longevity and growth, strengthening local economies.

Building on its proven US track record, Reins is poised to reshape how Canadian private businesses approach employee engagement and legacy planning. It's an empowering proposition: grow, succeed, and reward, all while keeping the reins firmly in the hands of the founders.
keyTakeaways: Reins, a US tech firm, has expanded its innovative "synthetic equity" solutions to Canada.
Canadian private businesses can now retain key talent and plan for succession without owners relinquishing control.
The model allows businesses to offer ownership-like incentives, building on a successful track record south of the border.
author: Staff Writer
